title: npm Supply Chain Attack Hides Malware Inside Normal Package Code to Evade Detection
content_md: A new npm supply chain campaign is hiding malware inside ordinary JavaScript package code instead of using the usual preinstall or postinstall scripts. The approach allows malicious packages to appear clean during installation while activating only when developers use their functions. The campaign involves the malicious indexed-btree package, which impersonates the legitimate sorted-btree library. Researchers said the attackers had earned about 109 ETH, valued at roughly €230,933 at the time of reporting. The campaign remains active, and further details may emerge. Unlike many npm threats, the package has no suspicious lifecycle scripts in its package.json file. This can make it appear legitimate to developers and security tools that focus mainly on installation-time behavior. Instead, the malware is embedded in the package’s normal application logic. The malicious code is placed inside BTree.prototype.set , a core function likely to be executed during regular use of the library. When a specific condition is met, the function launches an obfuscated JavaScript loader named sharedLoad.min.js . NPM Malware Evades Detection The loader collects information from infected systems, including the operating system, device architecture, hostname, CPU details, memory data, and uptime. It then sends this information to attacker-controlled Slack and Telegram infrastructure. The malware also uses an Ethereum Sepolia testnet smart contract as a command-and-control channel.
